title: Rotate an array by K positions (reverse whole, reverse first K, reverse rest).
shortTitle: Rotate an Array by K Positions
keyPoints: Right rotation by K moves each element K places to the right with wrap-around.
First reduce K modulo the array length so rotations larger than n are handled correctly.
Triple reversal: reverse the whole array, reverse the first K elements, reverse the remaining elements.
Runs in O(n) time with O(1) extra space, making it the optimal in-place solution.
Reversing the whole array brings the last K elements to the front but in reverse; the two sub-reversals fix the order.
A copy-to-new-array approach uses O(n) extra space; rotating one step at a time K times is O(n * K).
Handle negative K by converting to the equivalent right rotation, and treat empty or single-element arrays as no-ops.

s1_definition.oneliner: Reduce K by the length, then reverse the whole array, reverse the first K, and reverse the rest.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Array rotation** – moves each element K places to the right, with elements falling off the end wrapping to the front.
- **Triple reversal** – reverse the entire array, then reverse the first K elements, then reverse the remaining n - K elements.
- **Modulo reduction** – `K = K % n` handles rotations larger than the array length.
- **O(n) time, O(1) space** – three in-place reversals with no auxiliary array.
- **Alternatives** – copying to a new array uses O(n) space; rotating one step at a time is O(n * K).
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India keeps a rolling window of Rajesh's recent daily balances, and at day-end it must shift the window so the newest days appear first. Imagine the days written on a strip of paper. The clerk flips the whole strip over, then flips just the first part back, then flips the rest. After three flips the strip shows the days rotated into the new arrangement, all done on one strip without copying to a new one.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Rotating an array right by K moves each element K places to the right with wrap-around. The elegant in-place approach is the triple reversal: reverse the whole array, then reverse the first K elements, then reverse the rest. It runs in O(n) time with O(1) space.

Always reduce K modulo the length first, because rotating by more than the length is the same as rotating by K mod n. Also normalize a negative K into the equivalent right rotation and treat empty or single-element arrays as no-ops.

The triple reversal works because the original array is two blocks `[A | B]` and you want `[B | A]`. Reversing the whole array gives `[B_rev | A_rev]`, reversing the first K fixes B, and reversing the rest fixes A. Compared with the alternatives, copying to a new array uses O(n) extra space and rotating one step at a time is O(n * K), so the triple reversal is the best in-place choice.

In a banking project at the National Bank of India, this rotates Rajesh's rolling window of daily closing balances at day-end so the trend chart aligns with a new reference day, doing it in place to avoid allocating a fresh array per customer per day.

Remember one sentence: Reduce K modulo n, then reverse the whole array, reverse the first K, and reverse the rest to rotate in O(n) time and O(1) space.
